post.summary: Capture fresh device settings as a preset
post.description: Read selected devices under their operation locks and return XML. This endpoint does not change device settings or store a preset file. Capture has a 60-second deadline and rejects missing observations, identity changes, incomplete inventories, and unrepresentable flows. Advertised unsupported audio controls are listed in omitted. Managed-device transport and non-audio channel capture remain unavailable in this native build. The save_preset MCP tool adds explicit confirmation and atomic named-file storage.

200.description: Fresh settings encoded as XML.

post.summary: Inspect, plan or apply device controls
post.description: Reads advertised Bluetooth and Dante AV panels through correlated direct requests. Analog level controls use the codec provider. Planning reads fresh prerequisites and lock state. Application sends each mutation once, followed by one correlated readback query with a bounded observation deadline. Transport receipt, observed effective state, persistence and media readiness are separate results. Unknown identities, managed panel transport, unsupported settings and missing fresh observations cannot authorize a write. No physical-media qualification is implied.

200.description: Current controls, read-only plan or verified result.

409.description: Unavailable control, changed precondition or unverified application. Commands already sent are never retried automatically.

post.summary: Plan a preset against fresh device observations
post.description: Read selected targets under their ordered operation locks and return a fresh, read-only plan. Every target is planned before any apply command can be sent. Each action reports change, unchanged, unsupported, unavailable, or ambiguous. Unknown fields are preserved as unsupported. Dependent flow plans distinguish observed audio state from prerequisite audio changes. A plan does not authorize a write. Planning has a 60-second deadline.

200.description: Fresh preset plan.

post.summary: Apply a confirmed preset in dependency order
post.description: Validate XML digest and target identity, acquire device locks in a consistent order, and build all fresh plans before the first write. Device names, audio settings, channel labels and flows precede subscriptions across selected devices; network interface changes follow routing. After a change, dependent actions are planned again from fresh observations, including actions initially unchanged. Unsupported or unavailable planned settings do not block unrelated supported actions, but prevent complete=true. Conflicting performance intents are marked ambiguous before execution. Execution stops after a failed or unverified command. Final fresh readback checks successful and unchanged actions after the sequence; later drift prevents complete=true and configuration storage. Configured network state is distinguished from effective state, including pending reboot. The worker owns execution after caller disconnect. The 180-second execution budget stops starting further commands; an already-started bounded command is allowed to finish its readback. Every command is sent once, without automatic replay. Parent and child journal records retain receipts, readback and uncertainty. No automatic reboot is performed. Managed transport remains unavailable in this native build.

200.description: Preset execution report; inspect complete and every operation outcome. HTTP 200 alone does not establish application success.

post.summary: Measure a finite window of JACK audio
post.description: Targets map result names to source audio output ports. Each target measures the actual combined signal at an owned input. Duplicate source names are counted once. Duration defaults to 0.5 seconds and is clamped to 0.05 through 5 seconds; the worker captures ceil(duration * sample_rate) frames. Requests accept up to 32 targets and 2048 total distinct source connections across targets. Missing or non-audio ports produce target errors. Source changes, xruns, lost frame continuity, unavailable JACK, or a stalled worker fail the request. The worker never starts JACK. Consumer cancellation releases its inputs. Zero amplitude is represented by null decibel values.

getting-started.title: Getting started
paragraphs: Use the daemon origin that you already trust, then GET /server-info and GET /devices. Device selectors should use exact server names or context-qualified inventory IDs; percent-encode the entire selector as one path segment.
Open GET /events for a coherent initial snapshot and subsequent changes. A cached device record is presentation evidence; commands perform their own capability and freshness checks.

Download /openapi.json for client generation and contract inspection. Request payloads use JSON unless OAuth explicitly documents form encoding. Optional unknown fields are not evidence that a device supports a capability.

The existing CLI and browser retain their established request shapes, including the documented query filters. New interfaces use canonical path resources and typed request bodies. Selectors must remain a single percent-encoded path segment; the API version is selected by header, not a query parameter.

HTTP and HTTPS work without MCP. MCP is disabled by default. To enable its endpoint, OAuth routes and app sessions, set mcp = true in the [daemon] table of config.toml and restart the daemon. The mcp.enabled field in /server-info reports the running configuration. Disabled endpoints return 404 and service discovery omits the MCP path.

security.title: Authentication and trust
paragraphs: Ordinary REST device, diagnostics, journal and settings routes currently have no bearer authentication middleware. /device-lock-key returns a configured secret. Network access to these routes grants their capabilities. OAuth protects /mcp; it does not implicitly protect the rest of the server.

MCP accepts an explicitly configured static bearer token or OAuth authorization-code access tokens. OAuth requires PKCE S256. The netaudio:read scope permits reads; netaudio:write permits writes. Follow advertised OAuth metadata and store credentials securely.

TLS trust is independent of authentication. Configure a trusted certificate or explicit client trust. /shutdown additionally requires the actual socket peer to be loopback; forwarded headers do not satisfy that check.

events.title: Event stream and recovery
paragraphs: The /events response is text/event-stream. Each data field is a JSON object whose event field identifies its payload. The stream starts with snapshot, acquired coherently with subscription registration. Apply device_discovered and device_updated by stable server_name; device_patch merges changed fields and removes the named removed fields. device_removed deletes that identity from the client inventory.

patches=1 opts into incremental device patches. meters=0 excludes meter traffic. telemetry=0 excludes telemetry values but retains selected field-name notices; telemetry=none excludes both values and notices. A comma-separated telemetry selection includes only those known telemetry fields.

There is no Last-Event-ID replay. On disconnect, reconnect and replace the read model from the new coherent snapshot. Slow consumers are disconnected instead of silently dropping durable updates. Replaceable meter observations may be coalesced. Use /event-journal to recover durable historical records, including explicit observation gaps.

The snapshot source_generation identifies this in-memory producer lifetime. Every event has a decimal-string revision from that producer. Preserve all digits. Device changes retain publication order; filtered events leave revision gaps, and several projections may share a revision. Coalesced meter values may arrive out of global revision order but retain the newest observation for each meter identity. A revision is not a replay cursor. A new connection always begins with a replacement snapshot, even within the same generation.

commands.title: Command results and uncertainty
paragraphs: Requested, accepted, executed and observed state are different facts. 202 or accepted=true does not prove a physical result. Read the endpoint-specific confirmation fields, such as state_verified, configuration_confirmed, effective_state_confirmation and persistence_confirmation.

A timeout can happen after a command reached the device. outcome_unknown, change_sent, partial receiver acknowledgements and missing readback must be preserved. Do not automatically retry toggles, maintenance or other uncertain physical actions. Inspect fresh state before deciding what to do next.

Direct REST commands and MCP have different confirmation interfaces. MCP confirmable tools issue a preview token bound to the client, exact arguments and relevant device facts. Transmit-flow REST creation/deletion separately require confirmed=true. Sample-rate contraction separately uses confirm_destructive.

versioning.title: Public API version 1 and compatibility
paragraphs: This is stable public API major version 1, contract revision 1.0.0. The NetAudio-API-Version response header identifies the selected major. Send NetAudio-API-Version: 1 to pin a request; another value returns HTTP 406 before dispatch. Duplicate version headers return HTTP 400. Omission selects 1 on the existing routes and will continue to mean 1. Browser clients on another origin can read the exposed response header and /api descriptor without supplying a custom request header.

GET /api, GET /server-info and the initial event snapshot publish public_api metadata. Their existing version and api_version feature revision 3 fields keep their earlier meaning and are not the stable API major. Application version, source build identity, MCP protocol version and API contract revision are separate identifiers.

Compatible additions and fixes stay within major 1. Clients must ignore unknown object fields and unknown event kinds, preserve unknown enum values where a schema explicitly permits extension, and inspect capabilities before commands. Closed enums, required fields, units, nullability, identifier meanings, errors, authentication and event recovery are compatibility boundaries. New required inputs, removals and changed meanings require a new major when incompatible.

A future incompatible major requires an explicit selector, migration documentation and a declared support or retirement policy. It cannot silently change what these unqualified routes or header value 1 mean. An additive contract revision does not require a new major.

The daemon, HTTP, MCP, OAuth, discovery, monitoring and host-audio workers are native Rust. The CLI remains Python and the existing browser assets remain JavaScript. The contract documents implemented behavior; hardware capabilities and real-device qualification remain distinct from API compatibility.

history.title: Durable history and identifiers
paragraphs: /event-journal returns newest-first records with monotonic sequence identities. Use next_before_sequence as the next request cursor. A configured retention_limit is the default view window, not permission to discard stored events. Clearing the journal preserves monotonic sequence allocation.

/issues retains separate open and resolved episodes. Observation state observed/unobservable describes available evidence; it is not the same as issue lifecycle. Continue with the opaque next_cursor when returned.

SAP/SDP session_id and session_version are decimal strings in browser-facing representations. Preserve all digits; do not round them through a JavaScript Number. Timestamps retain their declared representation: ISO8601 strings for journal records, and Unix seconds for specific received telemetry fields.
